items.title: A dependent product of n-types over an arbitrary type is an n-type

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.9 at source lines 171-174: if every B(a) is an n-type then prd x:A B(x) is an n-type, for arbitrary A. The proof (source lines 176-185) is an induction whose step is not a direct application of the hypothesis: to show that f = g is an n-type one must first pass from the identity type of two dependent functions to the product prd a:A (f(a) = g(a)), which uses function extensionality (source line 183), and then apply closure under equivalence before the inductive hypothesis can be used on the pointwise path spaces (line 184). The base case at line 178 is a separate input, and the statement itself says nothing about how the path space of a function type is to be rewritten.
